svg.aria-label: Diagram: moving Azure resources, showing that a move changes the resource ID but not the region, the six checks that must pass before a move including no read-only lock and the resource provider being registered in the destination, the four-hour lock on both source and destination resource groups with its two phases and partial-completion outcome, the things that do not move such as role assignments, and the common error codes with what each one actually means
svg.title: An Azure resource move is a four-hour distributed operation that changes every resource ID and leaves role assignments behind
svg.text: A move is not a rename. It is a four-hour operation that can finish halfway.
It changes the identity of every resource involved, leaves access behind, and locks two resource groups while it decides.
What changes
The resource ID. Subscription and resource group are
both segments of it, so anything holding that string
— dashboards, scripts, templates, alerts, monitors —
points at something that no longer exists.
What does not change
The physical region. Moving a resource only changes its
associated resource group.
Existing resources stay fully operational throughout —
a virtual machine keeps serving traffic.
Six gates before the move starts, each with its own failure
Same Entra tenant
Source and destination subscriptions must share a tenant ID, and both must be active
No read-only lock
On the source, the destination resource group, or the subscription — post #22’s ReadOnly blocks moves
Provider registered
The destination subscription must be registered for the resource provider being moved
Quota headroom
The destination must not be pushed past its own limits by what arrives
Permissions on both ends
moveResources/action at the source, resourceGroups/write at the destination
Dependents travel together
Across subscriptions, a resource and its dependents must be in one group and move as one
Only top-level resources go in the request. Children move with their parent and cannot be moved on their own.
The four-hour lock, and why a move can end halfway
Both the source and the destination resource group are locked for the duration. No creating, no deleting, no property changes —
including resizing a virtual machine that is not part of the move. Neither group can join another move at the same time.
Phase one moves the resources. Phase two notifies the resource providers that depend on them. A failure in either phase can
hold the lock for the full four hours while Resource Manager retries.
After four hours both groups unlock. What moved is in the destination; what failed is still in the source. The estate is now split.
What the move leaves behind
Role assignments do not move. An assignment on a moved resource is orphaned and must be created again — the guidance is to
remove it deliberately beforehand rather than let the system clean it up afterwards.
A resource group itself cannot move to another subscription. You move its contents into a group that already exists there, and
tags, role assignments and policies do not transfer with them. Those are reapplied by hand.
Three error codes and what each one is really telling you
MissingMoveDependentResources
the dependency graph is wider than the request — one VM can need seven types
RequestDisallowedByPolicy
a policy at the destination denies creating what is arriving; validation runs policy too
MoveCannotProceedWithResourcesNot
a virtual network drags in every resource depending on it, including ones outside
InSucceededState
both resource groups and outside the move. Sources: Microsoft Learn, move-resource-group-and-subscription.
